page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge delivers moderate, balanced capabilities. While single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and poor single-threaded compression/decompression metrics, its multi-core scaling is average. Multi-threaded operations, such as stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 decompression, fall into the middle tier of performance. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks remains average, supporting steady data throughput. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also demonstrate consistent, mid-range performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density make this instance a stable option for workloads requiring predictable multi-core execution without the premium of high-frequency compute or massive memory arrays. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as medium-scale web serving, multi-threaded application servers, database operations, and moderate caching layers. However, it is less suitable for single-thread-bound tasks or heavy LLM inference workloads, where its performance is notably weaker.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data shows average multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operation speeds, though single-core execution and single-threaded compression tasks are relatively weak. With a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, the ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge offers a stable, cost-effective profile for multi-threaded applications, mid-sized databases, and general web serving.
